stem: Encapsulated Haemophilus influenzae strains are classified into how many polysaccharide capsule serotypes?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Confuses the typeable-versus-nontypeable split with the number of capsular serotypes.
options.explanation: H. influenzae splits into encapsulated (typeable) and nontypeable strains, but the capsule itself comes in six serotypes, a through f.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Undercounts the capsular serotypes of H. influenzae.
options.explanation: Four matches no H. influenzae classification; the polysaccharide capsule has six serotypes, designated a through f.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Undercounts the serotypes by one; there are six, a through f.
options.explanation: Five omits one type; the six capsular serotypes run a through f, and type b caused most invasive disease before vaccination.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Overcounts the capsular serotypes of H. influenzae.
options.explanation: Eight overcounts; the capsular serotypes of H. influenzae stop at f, giving six in total.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None — H. influenzae has six capsular serotypes, a through f.
options.explanation: CDC: H. influenzae has six different polysaccharide capsule serotypes (a-f); type b caused 95% of invasive disease before vaccines.

context: Learning objective: Haemophilus influenzae has six polysaccharide capsule serotypes (a-f); type b caused 95% of invasive disease before vaccination.
